title: Divergence Trace
description: IDEATE-stage artifact recording the six divergence operators run over the frozen DISCOVER material BEFORE any idea was proposed (constraint classification, assumption negation, problem reformulation, mechanism cross-product, enabler window, tension synthesis). Produced by the divergence-operator-runner seat, or by the idea proposer itself in a lighter run that does not dispatch that seat. MEASUREMENT ONLY: this artifact never cuts an idea, never ranks, and never gates a stage — it exists so that 'we diverged before we proposed' is an inspectable object rather than a claim. An operator that yielded nothing is recorded as an empty array, which is a finding, not a failure. An entry whose candidate falls outside the run's north-star topic boundary carries out_of_north_star:true so the director sees it and decides whether to widen the run; the worker never executes such a candidate on its own.

trace_id.description: Short unique identifier for this trace, e.g. DT-001. Non-blank.

produced_by.description: Which seat authored the trace: divergence-operator-runner (independent seat) or hypothesis-generator (proposer fallback).

constraints.description: Operator 1 — constraint classification. Every constraint the current approach carries, typed hard / soft / hidden, with the system that dropping it would produce.

if_dropped.description: The system this would produce, or 'nothing coherent'.

negations.description: Operator 2 — assumption negation. Each settled assumption negated, WITH the one-sentence system sketch that the negation implies; a negation with no system attached is not usable.

conditions_changed.description: Only meaningful when verdict is already_explored: what has changed since the conditions that killed it.

reformulations.description: Operator 3 — problem reformulation. Each restatement changes exactly ONE thing (objective / formalism / granularity / agent / timescale / direction).

cross_product.description: Operator 4 — mechanism cross-product against a deliberately distant field. `transfers` distinguishes a real mechanism transfer from vocabulary borrowing; vocabulary_only entries are kept as recorded discards, never promoted.

enablers.description: Operator 5 — enabler window. What became newly available (data / model / hardware / cost / tool / regulation / published result), including the machine's OWN registered hardware, and what each newly permits. `window` records the timing read: too_early (technology does not exist yet), sweet_spot (feasible in the last 6-18 months), probably_done (equally doable five years ago).

tensions.description: Operator 6 — tension synthesis. Both sides of a real trade-off plus the system that would achieve both at once. is_compromise:true marks an entry that merely splits the difference, which is a compromise rather than an idea.

synthesis.description: A system achieving both sides, or 'none found'.

opposition_is_formalization_artifact.description: true / false / 'unknown': whether the opposition is an artifact of how the problem was formalized rather than a fact about the world.

anomalies.description: The anomaly-first pass that precedes the operators: observations the field's current explanation does not account for, each with COMPETING candidate mechanisms and the discriminating evidence that would separate them. Abduction, not selection among known answers.

operators_run.description: Which operators were actually run, including any that produced nothing (their array is then empty). Honesty record: a missing operator and an empty operator are different facts.

notes.description: Optional caveats (e.g. which DISCOVER artifacts were absent this run).
